title: Darrowshire: Lost and Remembered
summary: Pamela’s search follows a ruined village’s divided accounts, the relatives and relics that preserve them, and Chromie’s attempt to revisit the battle that broke the Redpath family.
opening: A child in the ruins asks after her family. Her question leads through a village’s torn history, where one book gives a date the wider war will not accept and a later spell offers a limited answer.

chapters.title: The fall of Darrowshire
chapters.body:
When the Scourge reached Darrowshire, a small village stood before a ruin greater than its defenders could foresee. Its last battle would endure in a troubled memory, with even the age of its fall disputed. Beyond that uncertainty remained a loss that no date could lessen: homes destroyed, families broken, and the dead unable to leave what had been taken from them.

Horgus the Ravager came among the Scourge that threatened Darrowshire. Captain Joseph Redpath and Davil led the village’s defense. The settlement they guarded was a fragile home, held against a force that brought the wider war into its fields. Those who stood there fought for familiar doors and faces; the invaders carried a danger that would reach beyond the living.

Davil struck Horgus down, then died of his own wounds. The village had lost a defender even as one of its enemies fell. His courage would survive him in Darrowshire’s memory, and a libram bearing his name would later draw the living back toward that sacrifice. Victory over the Ravager had come at a cost the village could not replace.

After Davil fell, Marduk the Black corrupted Joseph Redpath. The captain who had led Darrowshire’s defense became a danger to his own people. The village was destroyed. What had begun as resistance ended in betrayal through a will taken by the enemy, leaving the survivors’ memory burdened by the fate of the man who had stood for their protection.

Marlene remembered hiding Pamela when the fighting came. The child’s small place within that memory stood against the vastness of Darrowshire’s ruin. War had reached the family’s home, and concealment had offered only a fragile hope. In the years that followed, Pamela would remain among the village’s spirits, still bound to the people and the world she had lost.

chapters.title: Pamela’s family
chapters.body:
Long after the battle, Marlene’s wandering spirit asked for help finding Pamela. The Plaguelands had become a country of ruined homes and unresting dead. Darrowshire’s loss endured there beyond the reach of its enemies’ first assault. A stranger’s search began among those remnants, seeking a child whom the family still remembered and an answer the village had never found.

Pamela waited among the ruined homes of Darrowshire. Her doll was missing, its parts scattered through the broken settlement. The visitor gathered them for her. Beside a catastrophe that had destroyed a village, the small keepsake offered a gentler measure of loss: a child still waiting, and something once familiar brought back into her hands.

With the doll restored, Pamela asked about her parents and the home she remembered. The little gift could answer one absence, but not the others. Her questions led the visitor onward toward relatives and the remnants of the past. In the quiet of the ruined village, the child’s hope reached beyond what the living could yet explain.

Marlene knew Pamela had died, and Joseph’s fate led back toward the corrupted captain of Darrowshire’s defense. Yet she could not bring herself to tell the child the whole truth. Grief held the answer unspoken. One spirit waited for her family; another carried knowledge too painful to give, and the visitor stood between the child’s longing and the aunt’s sorrow.

A wedding ring turned the search toward Chromie in Andorhal. The bronze dragon wore the form of a gnome historian among the ruined town’s remains. A small token of the Redpath family now lay beside a greater interest in Darrowshire’s past. The questions Pamela had asked could no longer be answered by keepsakes alone; they led toward the battle itself.

chapters.title: Witnesses and relics
chapters.body:
The Annals preserved Darrowshire’s last battle, but their date did not agree with the remembered age of the Scourge’s assault. The village’s history had reached the living imperfectly. Within those troubled pages endured the names of defenders and enemies, and the change that had overtaken Joseph. Chromie’s search had to pass through that uncertain memory to reach the family’s unfinished grief.

At Light’s Hope Chapel, Carlin remembered the people of Darrowshire. The village’s fallen defenders were still bound in Scourge service, and he asked that they be freed. Their suffering had outlasted the battle that killed them. Among the open fields of the Plaguelands, the search became an act of release for those who had once stood against the invaders.

The trail turned toward relics of Darrowshire’s enemies: a skull associated with Horgus and a broken sword with Marduk. From different places in the Plaguelands, the objects were brought into the search. They offered material traces of the ruin remembered in the Annals. The village’s lost battle was drawing nearer through what its foes had left behind.

At Hearthglen, Davil’s libram carried a trace of the fallen defender into the search. The fortified town stood far from the home he had died defending. A book could not return him to Darrowshire, yet his memory endured within its recovery. Beside the relics of the village’s enemies, the living now gathered something belonging to one who had resisted them.

Joseph Redpath’s broken shield was found near the ruined farm of Gahrron’s Withering. Its damage offered no answer to every part of his fall. Yet the object recalled the captain before corruption had turned him against his people. Among leaning buildings and pallid fields, another remnant of Darrowshire’s defense returned to the hands gathering its history.

A mystic crystal responded to skulls from Scourge that had taken part in the assault. Alongside the Annals and the relics of the fallen, those remains added another thread to Chromie’s work. The battle’s memory was being gathered from enemies and defenders alike. What the village could no longer tell in living voices endured in fragments awaiting her spell.

Carlin supplied the fuller account, and the gathered relics returned to Chromie. She prepared a spell through which the battle could be revisited and its consequences confronted. The family’s search had passed from Pamela’s doll to the memory of a village at war. Now the living would enter that memory, carrying what they had recovered toward the losses it preserved.

chapters.title: The battle revisited
chapters.body:
Chromie’s spell opened a remembered Darrowshire beneath the shadow of battle. The visitor entered that past to help its defenders. Davil had to endure until Horgus fell; Joseph’s corruption still had to be faced. The village’s old ruin remained the wound from which this journey had begun. Within the spell, its unfinished struggle demanded another answer.

In the remembered battle, Davil stood against Horgus once more. With the visitor’s help, he endured until the Ravager was slain. The fatal pattern preserved in the Annals had been interrupted within Chromie’s spell. Yet Darrowshire’s danger had not ended with that foe. Joseph still stood within reach of the corruption that had once turned the defense against itself.

Joseph survived long enough to fall beneath corruption, and the visitor faced him as Redpath the Corrupted. Saving Davil could not spare the captain that change. The remembered battle now required that Joseph’s hostile form be defeated. Beyond the clash remained the man Pamela awaited, held apart from his family by the ruin that had overtaken their village.

After the fighting, Joseph’s spirit came to Pamela. The child spoke as though her father would come home, and entrusted the visitor with a key to a chest behind the house. What Chromie’s spell might mean for the lasting course of time remained uncertain. Yet within the remembered village, father and child met again, and the long search closed upon a small welcome.
